newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian metals chief wants gold sector changes.
newsitem.headline: New Russian metals chief wants gold sector changes.

text.p: A senior Russian official said on Tuesday Russia's gold market needs radical, market-economy changes to survive, and called for the creation of a giant gold corporation.

Vladimir Piskunov, head of the Industry Ministry's precious metals and precious stones section, said he wanted to implement extensive market-economy reforms in gold mining but to keep some controls in place.
"The market is in a state of stagnation," Piskunov said. "It's obvious the system needs serious rethinking and serious re-orientation."
The ministry's department has assumed some of the functions of the defunct State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones (Komdragmet), disbanded by presidential decree in August.
The section handles output issues and some aspects of exports, while the Finance Ministry deals with the main export and reserves issues.

A ministry news release said it made sense to merge the 650 or more gold mining companies that emerged during privatisation into one transnational company like natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom or diamond group Almazy Rossii-Sakha.
It said private financing could double gold output to 240-250 tonnes a year and estimated the amount of outside investment needed at $3 billion.
Piskunov had no details on what the ministry's department planned for output of platinum, palladium and platinum group metals for 1997 and said he was not a specialist in those areas.
He said Russian gold output in 1995 slipped to 122 tonnes and would decline further this year. Some independent specialists say 1996 output could fall to around 100 tonnes.
Piskunov said the Central Bank was putting the breaks on development of the gold sector by offering to mines to buy all their output but not to pre-finance it.
"The Central Bank has said it is ready to buy all gold mined in Russia, but without advancing payment for its production. They just cannot finance output, and it's a vicious circle.

"The banks don't have any way to get their gold to markets," he said, referring to laws that make it practically impossible for banks to export gold. "We need to develop a mechanism by which gold can become a real financial instrument."
